name: craftplan
description: Self-hosted software for managing artisanal D2C micro-businesses
readmeExcerpt:
Craftplan

Open-source ERP for small-scale artisanal manufacturers and craft businesses

Craftplan brings all essential business tools into one platform: catalog management, inventory control, order processing, production planning, purchasing, and CRM, so you can get off the ground quickly without paying for multiple separate platforms. ## Features **Catalog & BOM** - Product catalog with photos and labels - Versioned Bills of Materials — edit latest, older versions read-only - Automatic cost rollups across nested BOMs - Labor steps with time and cost tracking **Orders & Invoices** - Customer order processing with calendar-based scheduling - Invoice generation - Order item allocation to production batches **Production** - Production batching with automatic material consumption - Cost snapshots per batch - Completion workflow with produced quantity tracking **Inventory** - Raw material management with lot traceability - Stock movements (consume, receive, adjust) - Allergen and nutritional fact tracking - Demand forecasting and reorder planning **Purchasing** - Purchase orders and supplier management - Receiving into stock with lot creation **CRM** - Customer and supplier database - Order history and statistics **Import / Export** - CSV bulk import for products, materials, and customers - CSV export **Email** - Transactional email delivery configurable from the UI - SMTP, SendGrid, Mailgun, Postmark, Brevo, and Amazon SES - API keys encrypted at rest **Calendar Feed** - iCal (.ics) subscription URL for Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, or any iCal-compatible app - Includes order deliveries and production batch schedules - Generate and revoke feeds from Settings **API** - JSON:API and GraphQL endpoints for programmatic access - API key authentication with encrypted storage - CORS configuration **Access Control** - Admin and staff roles - Policy-based authorization on all resources **Global Search** - Command palette (`Cmd+K` / `Ctrl+K`) for instant access to any record - Fuzzy search across products, materials, orders, customers, and batches ## Screenshots
## Tech Stack Elixir · [Ash Framework](https://ash-hq.org/) · Phoenix LiveView · PostgreSQL · Tailwind CSS ## Getting Started Deploy Craftplan on your own server. No need to clone the repo: ```bash curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/puemos/craftplan/main/docker-compose.yml curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/puemos/craftplan/main/.env.example cp .env.example .env # Fill in the required secrets (see .env.example) docker compose up -d ``` This starts Craftplan, PostgreSQL, and SeaweedFS with database migrations running automatically. **Upgrading from MinIO?** The updated Compose file automatically migrates and verifies existing photos before starting Craftplan. Later SeaweedFS upgrades skip migration. Keep your `.env` and volumes; see the [upgrade guide](docs/src/pages/docs/storage-migration.md) for disk-space requirements and recovery. See the [self-hosting guide](https://puemos.github.io/craftplan/docs/self-hosting/) for single-container mode, Railway deployment, reverse proxy setup, and more. ## Development Setup > For contributors who want to work on the codebase. **Prerequisites:** Docker and [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/) ```bash mise install # Install Elixir, Erlang/OTP, and Node.js versions from mise.toml mise run services:up # Start PostgreSQL + SeaweedFS + Mailpit mise run setup # Install deps, migrate, build assets, seed mise run dev # Start at localhost:4000 ``` See the [development setup guide](https://puemos.github.io/craftplan/docs/getting-started/) for detailed instructions. ## Why Craftplan? - **Purpose-built for artisanal manufacturing** — not a generic ERP adapted to fit; workflows are designed around small-batch, made-to-order production - **Allergen & nutritional tracking** — first-class support for food and beverage producers who need to track ingredients and generate nutrition labels - **BOM versioning with cost rollups** — iterate on recipes and formulas while keeping full history and accurate costing - **Self-hosted, no vendor lock-in** — your data stays on your infrastructure, backed by PostgreSQL ## Documentation - [Full documentation](https://puemos.github.io/craftplan/docs/) - [API reference (JSON:API & GraphQL)](https://puemos.github.io/craftplan/docs/api/) ## Contributing Contributions are welcome. For major changes, please [open an issue](https://github.com/puemos/craftplan/issues) first to discuss your proposal. ```bash mise run test # Run the test suite mise run format # Format code (Styler, Spark, Tailwind, HEEx) mise run format:check # Check formatting without modifying files mise run ci # Run the full CI suite locally (requires services:up) ``` Commits follow the convention: `type(scope): description` (e.g., `feat(batching):`, `fix(orders):`, `ui(production):`). ## License This project is licensed under the AGPLv3 License. See the [LICENSE](LICENSE) file for details. ## Support - [Open an issue](https://github.com/puemos/craftplan/issues) - [Read the docs](https://puemos.github.io/craftplan/docs/)
readmeHtml:
Craftplan

Open-source ERP for small-scale artisanal manufacturers and craft businesses

Craftplan brings all essential business tools into one platform: catalog management, inventory control, order processing, production planning, purchasing, and CRM, so you can get off the ground quickly without paying for multiple separate platforms.

Features

Catalog & BOM

  • Product catalog with photos and labels
  • Versioned Bills of Materials — edit latest, older versions read-only
  • Automatic cost rollups across nested BOMs
  • Labor steps with time and cost tracking

Orders & Invoices

  • Customer order processing with calendar-based scheduling
  • Invoice generation
  • Order item allocation to production batches

Production

  • Production batching with automatic material consumption
  • Cost snapshots per batch
  • Completion workflow with produced quantity tracking

Inventory

  • Raw material management with lot traceability
  • Stock movements (consume, receive, adjust)
  • Allergen and nutritional fact tracking
  • Demand forecasting and reorder planning

Purchasing

  • Purchase orders and supplier management
  • Receiving into stock with lot creation

CRM

  • Customer and supplier database
  • Order history and statistics

Import / Export

  • CSV bulk import for products, materials, and customers
  • CSV export

Email

  • Transactional email delivery configurable from the UI
  • SMTP, SendGrid, Mailgun, Postmark, Brevo, and Amazon SES
  • API keys encrypted at rest

Calendar Feed

  • iCal (.ics) subscription URL for Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, or any iCal-compatible app
  • Includes order deliveries and production batch schedules
  • Generate and revoke feeds from Settings

API

  • JSON:API and GraphQL endpoints for programmatic access
  • API key authentication with encrypted storage
  • CORS configuration

Access Control

  • Admin and staff roles
  • Policy-based authorization on all resources

Global Search

  • Command palette (Cmd+K / Ctrl+K) for instant access to any record
  • Fuzzy search across products, materials, orders, customers, and batches

Screenshots

Tech Stack

Elixir · Ash Framework · Phoenix LiveView · PostgreSQL · Tailwind CSS

Getting Started

Deploy Craftplan on your own server. No need to clone the repo:

curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/puemos/craftplan/main/docker-compose.yml
curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/puemos/craftplan/main/.env.example
cp .env.example .env   # Fill in the required secrets (see .env.example)
docker compose up -d

This starts Craftplan, PostgreSQL, and SeaweedFS with database migrations running automatically.

Upgrading from MinIO? The updated Compose file automatically migrates and verifies existing photos before starting Craftplan. Later SeaweedFS upgrades skip migration. Keep your .env and volumes; see the upgrade guide for disk-space requirements and recovery.

See the self-hosting guide for single-container mode, Railway deployment, reverse proxy setup, and more.

Development Setup

For contributors who want to work on the codebase. Prerequisites: Docker and mise

mise install            # Install Elixir, Erlang/OTP, and Node.js versions from mise.toml
mise run services:up    # Start PostgreSQL + SeaweedFS + Mailpit
mise run setup          # Install deps, migrate, build assets, seed
mise run dev            # Start at localhost:4000

See the development setup guide for detailed instructions.

Why Craftplan?

  • Purpose-built for artisanal manufacturing — not a generic ERP adapted to fit; workflows are designed around small-batch, made-to-order production
  • Allergen & nutritional tracking — first-class support for food and beverage producers who need to track ingredients and generate nutrition labels
  • BOM versioning with cost rollups — iterate on recipes and formulas while keeping full history and accurate costing
  • Self-hosted, no vendor lock-in — your data stays on your infrastructure, backed by PostgreSQL

Documentation

  • Full documentation
  • API reference (JSON:API & GraphQL)

Contributing

Contributions are welcome. For major changes, please open an issue first to discuss your proposal.

mise run test          # Run the test suite
mise run format        # Format code (Styler, Spark, Tailwind, HEEx)
mise run format:check  # Check formatting without modifying files
mise run ci            # Run the full CI suite locally (requires services:up)

Commits follow the convention: type(scope): description (e.g., feat(batching):, fix(orders):, ui(production):).

License

This project is licensed under the AGPLv3 License. See the LICENSE file for details.

Support

  • Open an issue
  • Read the docs

releases.name: v0.7.7 — Dependency and security update
releases.body:
Updates application dependencies, documentation tooling, runtimes, and release infrastructure across Craftplan.

- Update Ash to 3.37.2, AshPostgres to 2.15.2, Phoenix to 1.8.16, and LiveView to 1.2.13, including upstream authorization, validation, and URL-handling security fixes.
- Upgrade Elixir to 1.20.4 and Erlang/OTP to 28.5.0.8. Replace end-of-life Node 20 with Node 24.22.2. Move application images to Debian 13 and ncurses 6.
- Upgrade Money, Ecto, admin, storage clients, Astro, React, Tailwind, esbuild, and compatible transitive dependencies. Money formatting now uses Localize in place of the removed CLDR backend.
- Update SeaweedFS to 4.51, rclone to 1.75.2, and the legacy migration binary. Rebuild storage tools with patched Go, JOSE, Chi, and x/net dependencies.
- Update the vendored topbar 2 progress bar to managed topbar 3.0.1.
- Add dependency audits, Phoenix static analysis, documentation builds, and image vulnerability gates for fixable high/critical advisories to CI. Pin GitHub Actions to reviewed release commits.

Validation:

- 465 application tests passed with the standard parallel runner, plus all five isolated SMTP tests (one existing application test remains sk

releases.name: v0.7.6 — Modals that fit the viewport
releases.body:
## Fixes

- Fixed tall modals being clipped and impossible to scroll at viewport widths of 640px and above, including Create Customer and Create Product (#58).
- Dialogs now fit within the viewport and scroll internally at every width. Titles, close buttons, and separate footer actions remain visible.

Validated with the application test suite and browser checks covering customer and product forms, the 640px breakpoint, short windows, import footer actions, and the fullscreen Make Sheet.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/puemos/craftplan/compare/v0.7.5...v0.7.6

releases.name: v0.7.5 — Native intermediate production
releases.body:
## Native intermediate production

Make a material once, stock its output, and use that stock across finished products. The new **Production** tab supports versioned recipes, scaled batch planning, input-lot selection, and recording actual yield and usage.

- Complete a batch to consume its source lots and stock the output atomically; insufficient or unavailable stock rejects the transaction.
- Calculate the produced lot’s unit cost from actual inputs. Finished products consume that stocked lot without consuming the raw materials again.
- Preserve each completed batch’s original recipe, yield, cost, and input lots when future recipes change.
- Trace supplier lots through intermediates to finished products and customer orders, or trace finished batches back to their original sources. CSV exports include the intermediate links.

[Workflow guide with the new demo and screenshots](https://puemos.github.io/craftplan/docs/intermediates/)

## Upgrading

This release adds material recipe, production batch, and input-lot tables. Standard Docker startup runs migrations automatically. Custom release deployments should run `bin/migrate` before starting the new version.

Validated with 464 pass

releases.name: v0.7.4
releases.body:
## Fixes

- Cancel open or in-progress production batches before material consumption. Cancellation returns their order quantities to the planner; completed or consumed batches remain protected. (#47, #51)
- Print ordinary decimal quantities on production batch sheets by default. General Settings can enable scientific notation when preferred. (#48, #52)
- Resolve allergens through nested subassemblies and include nested materials in recipe rollups, consumption requirements, and frozen batch declarations. (#49, #53)

## Documentation

- Explain how to model produced and stocked intermediates shared by several finished products, avoid duplicate raw-material consumption, and use a lot-aware manual workaround. Automatic production into intermediate inventory and upstream lot genealogy are not implemented by this release. (#50, #54)

## Upgrading

This release includes a settings database migration for the batch-sheet notation preference. The standard Docker startup runs migrations automatically; custom release deployments should run `bin/migrate` before starting the new version.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/puemos/craftplan/compare/v0.7.3...v0.7.4

releases.name: v0.7.3
releases.body:
## Fixes

- Adds visible **Edit order** links in Orders and customer order history.
- Allows fulfillment and payment status updates from the order form.
- Supports removing products while preserving the original order prices.
- Adds confirmed order deletion; production-linked orders remain protected to preserve traceability.

Resolves #44. Implemented in #46.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/puemos/craftplan/compare/v0.7.2...v0.7.3

aiSummary.oneLiner: An open-source ERP system built specifically for small-scale artisanal manufacturers.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Craftplan is a comprehensive, open-source Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system tailored specifically for small-scale artisanal manufacturers and direct-to-consumer (D2C) micro-businesses. Built on the highly concurrent Elixir ecosystem, it provides a robust backend capable of managing complex, multi-stage production workflows with real-time updates. The platform unifies inventory tracking, raw material procurement, and customer order fulfillment into a single, cohesive interface. It is uniquely designed to handle the variable, small-batch nature of craft businesses, accommodating custom product variations and unpredictable production timelines that traditional corporate ERPs fail to address. By offering a self-hosted solution under the AGPLv3 license, it empowers independent creators to maintain complete sovereignty over their critical business data.
keyFeatures: Artisanal Workflow Management: Specifically designed to track the unique, variable, and multi-stage production processes common in small-batch manufacturing.
Unified Inventory Tracking: Seamlessly links raw material procurement, current stock levels, and finished goods inventory into a single cohesive database.
Elixir Backend Architecture: Built on the highly concurrent Erlang VM (BEAM), ensuring massive scalability and real-time data updates across the application.
Direct-to-Consumer Fulfillment: Integrates order management directly with production schedules, ensuring that custom client requests are tracked from fabrication to shipping.
Self-Hosted Data Sovereignty: Provided as an open-source Docker container, allowing businesses to retain absolute control over their sensitive financial and customer data.
Custom Product Variation Support: Flexibly handles highly customized orders and unique product iterations without requiring rigid, predefined corporate SKU structures.

useCases.title: Managing Leathercraft Production
useCases.description: Independent leatherworkers can track their inventory of raw hides, hardware, and dyes while managing custom client wallet orders in real-time.

useCases.title: Scaling Micro-Breweries
useCases.description: Small-scale brewers can utilize the system to manage complex fermentation schedules, track grain inventory, and organize direct-to-consumer keg sales.

useCases.title: Organizing Custom Furniture Builds
useCases.description: Woodworkers can link raw lumber procurement directly to specific, multi-week client commissions, ensuring materials are always available when needed.

useCases.title: Tracking Ceramic Studio Inventory
useCases.description: Potters can manage the variable timelines of clay throwing, bisque firing, and glazing, while tracking their inventory of specialized chemical glazes.

useCases.title: Operating Independent Apparel Brands
useCases.description: Small clothing designers can track limited-run fabric supplies and coordinate sewing workflows alongside managing their online boutique orders.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: This ERP is built for small-scale manufacturers, food producers, and craft business owners who need precise inventory and production tracking. It requires basic knowledge of Docker for self-hosting.
